items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was me and a guy named Mel Mandel, who handled advertising, and there was a receptionist, and that was it.

ctx.x: Right. But, to stay there for a moment, you said “a regime of one.” What was the reality of the Down Beat office in 1950?

There was me and a guy named Mel Mandel, who handled advertising, and there was a receptionist, and that was it. Now the main office was in Chicago. The owner I think had a printing business. He had no interest in the music.
